item: GFN2-xTB energies, analytic gradients, atomic charges and dipoles against xtb 6.8.0, xtb 6.7.1 (the g-xTB 2.0.1 build) and tblite 0.8.0
Elements H–Rn, charges −3 to +3, spin multiplicities up to 11, open-shell transition-metal complexes
ALPB (25 solvents) and GBSA (14 solvents) in all three reference states; electronic temperatures 0–5000 K; SCF accuracies 1–1e-6

Semi-numerical Hessians and frequencies against xtb --hess; analytic Hessians against tightly converged references (8 benchmark systems, and 45 reference-matrix cases: closed and open shell, charges, transition metals, ALPB and GBSA in several solvents, high electronic temperature, all three conventions) and against xtb --hess; thread-count invariance; invalid inputs

Timings of GFN2-xTB and g-xTB energies, gradients and Hessians against xtb 6.8.0 and both g-xTB programs on an Intel laptop and a shared 64-core AMD node (3–600 atoms; energy + gradient on 1, 2, 4, 8 threads, Hessians on 1, 8), axtb with faer and with Intel MKL loaded at run time (and AMD AOCL on the node); earlier GFN2-xTB thread, batch and start-up runs on both machines
A GPU eigensolver (FP64, mixed and adaptive precision) on two GPUs without fast FP64, up to 6000 basis functions; it is kept on a separate branch, not in the main code

How the molecules were chosen: hand-picked test structures, generated water clusters and alkanes, and hand-built metal complexes. They are not optimized geometries and not a sample of any production workload.

g-xTB v1.1 and 2.0.1 against their programs for every element H–Lr (169 generated molecules each: hydrides, halides, oxides, aqua and ammine ions, radicals, f-shell high-spin), plus the reference sets
Energy differences (conformers, binding, SN2 and HCN → HNC barriers) under program and default g-xTB conventions, on structures optimized with each version

SCF restarts (each program's restart files reproduced), bond orders, HOMO–LUMO gaps and molecular quadrupoles against xtb 6.7.1, 6.8.0 and both g-xTB programs; restarts along random walks, geomeTRIC and Sella runs
g-xTB 2.0.1 energies and analytic gradients against the 2.0.1 program on its reference set across H–Lr, including f-shell molecules
g-xTB 2.0.1 analytic Hessians against tight references and the 2.0.1 program (9 systems including UF6, GdCl3 and ferrocene); memory and time up to a 600-atom water cluster
g-xTB 2.0.1 and v1.1 at 300, 1000, 3000 and 5000 K against both programs (59 and 16 molecules), energies, gradients and SCF iterations
g-xTB 2.0.1 in ALPB water through the composite correction, against the three xtb runs it replaces (9 structures, including two that need a retry at a higher electronic temperature)
Vibrational analysis and quasi-RRHO thermochemistry against xtb 6.7.1 and the g-xTB 2.0.1 program (7 molecules, linear and symmetric tops, a transition state)
Molden orbital files against the files of xtb, the g-xTB 2.0.1 program and g-xtb 1.1.0 (23 cases, s to f functions, open shells)

GFN-FF topology, charges, energies and gradients against xtb 6.8.0 and 6.7.1 --gfnff on 269 structures (H–Rn, charges −3 to +3, metal complexes, hydrogen- and halogen-bonded dimers, up to 640 atoms); Hessians on 10 structures; time and memory up to 9900 atoms

The solvation composite in solvents other than water, with GBSA or at other reference states; GFN-FF with implicit solvent or point charges (QM/MM electrostatic embedding); GFN1-xTB, periodic systems, CPCM-X and COSMO solvation, point charges
Geometry optimizations and molecular dynamics (axtb provides energies, gradients and Hessians; an outside optimizer drives them)
GFN2-xTB and g-xTB above 999 atoms (GFN-FF was run up to 9900); CPUs other than these two; macOS, Windows and ARM
